what: Context sentence "Don't vendor the vendor: the system is written by shadcn's own CLI, never by hand" — the declarations inside the generated `@theme inline` block of `client/src/index.css` are reflowed from `--name: value;` to `--name:value;` (whitespace only; values untouched, `:root`/`.dark` left exactly as the CLI wrote them, the components not edited at all).
why: M1/leg (b) asserts the bundled css contains the exact texts `--color-primary:var(--primary)` and `--radius-lg:var(--radius)` with no space after the colon. Bun's CSS printer copies a custom property's value text verbatim including its leading space, so the CLI's `--color-primary: var(--primary);` bundles spaced and leg (b) is red. Verified with a minimal repro (`--a:var(--x)` bundles unspaced, `--a: var(--x)` bundles spaced). The bundle is otherwise byte-identical to the probe the Context measured (162,042 css chars), so the Context's quoted literals dropped the space rather than the CLI's output differing — and the Machine clause's exact text is what the peer's exam asserts.

what: Context install order — `bun add tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite`, the tsconfig `paths` and the Vite plugin/alias were put in place *before* `shadcn init`, with a one-line `@import "tailwindcss";` seed at `client/src/index.css` that the CLI then overwrote with its own 130-line file.
why: The Context reads as though `shadcn init` is the first move, but the CLI's preflight refuses to run without a Tailwind config and a resolvable import alias ("No Tailwind CSS configuration found" / "Could not find valid path aliases"). The end state is exactly the one the Context describes; only the order differs. Separately, shadcn 4.21.0 did not rewrite `@types/node` this run — it is still `^26.4.1`, so the Context's "put it back" step was a no-op.

what: Context: "the two paths meet at the same `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`/`Input.insertText`/`Input.dispatchKeyEvent` calls" — a click on a control whose content box has zero area now goes through `DOM.resolveNode` + `Runtime.callFunctionOn` calling `click()` on the node in the page, instead of `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` at the box centre. Every control with a non-zero box still goes through the mouse, unchanged.
why: M2's third assertion cannot hold otherwise. Measured on the fleet's shell, M2's page gives the empty `<span role="checkbox" aria-label="walk the dog">` a box of `{x:279, y:9, width:0, height:19}`; a mouse event is delivered by hit test, a zero-width rect contains no point, so the press landed on `<html>` and `window.__hit` stayed `undefined`. Refusing such a control would make the accessibility tree's names useless for exactly the controls only a name can find (an `aria-label`led widget with no text, a library's visually hidden input). This is not specific to the role path — a string selector naming the same span missed it the same way, and has since task 1.
